days.reason: The day is directly named after the parable of the workers in the vineyard (Matt 20:1-16), which is the main text for this Sunday. The text illustrates God's grace and logic where 'the last shall be first'.

This passage (Matt 20:17-28) follows immediately after the parable of the vineyard and expands on the theme of service and leadership in God's kingdom, which is central to understanding the parable. It is often part of the reading for this day.

The conclusion of the chapter (Matt 20:29-34), with the healing of the two blind men, serves as a practical illustration of Jesus' service and God's grace, which are the main themes in the preceding passages. This passage is often included in the complete reading for the day.

In many reader editions and liturgical plans for Vineyard Sunday (or Sundays in Lent where this passage is read), the entire chapter 20 is included. Although the main theme (the vineyard and service) is covered in verses 1–28, the healing serves as a practical demonstration of God's grace and Jesus' service, which are central themes for the day. A secondary tag should be added for the remainder of the chapter for completeness.; [minor] Tagging verses 17–28 as 'secondary' is correct in relation to the main parable, but it is worth noting that this passage is often just as central in sermons as the parable itself.
